full_citation: Morris TP, White IR, Crowther MJ. Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods. Statistics in Medicine. 2019;38(11):2074-2102.
claim_supported: EXPLICIT SOURCE CLAIM: relative bias is defined only for true parameter |theta|>0 and is undefined by division-by-zero at theta=0; absolute bias is the standard alternative performance measure for boundary/zero true values.
exact_relevant_methodological_point: Also EXPLICIT: bias = (1/n_sim) sum(theta_hat_i) - theta; coverage = (1/n_sim) sum 1(theta_hat_low,i <= theta <= theta_hat_upp,i); MCSE(coverage) = sqrt(Coverage*(1-Coverage)/n_sim); the ADEMP framework requires missingness/non-convergence to be reported as the first performance measure and further measures treated tentatively if missingness is nontrivial.
model_assumptions: Frequentist simulation-study framework, i.i.d. replications indexed by n_sim, a single true parameter theta per scenario -- matches Model 3B's per-cell design (one true n_c per cell) closely.
applicability_to_model_3b: Directly applicable to OD-005 (AbsBias_c vs RelBias at n_c=0) and to OD-006's denominator question (n_sim in the source formula is the count of replications that YIELDED a result, i.e. structurally analogous to Model 3B's R_valid,c/R_metric,c, not R_attempted,c) -- see mapping table in WAVE_2_OD_005_006_015_MATHEMATICAL_EVIDENCE_REVIEW.md.
limitations: Paper does not discuss annual-resolution / small-N Hawkes-process recovery specifically; general simulation-study guidance, not point-process-specific. Does not explicitly mandate one universal denominator convention -- it recommends reporting missingness as its own measure and treating further measures 'tentatively' under nontrivial missingness, which is compatible with more than one downstream denominator choice.
supports_option: AbsBias_c (OD-005); Coverage_c (OD-006, via n_sim-as-valid-count structural analogy -- inferential, not an explicit statement about Model 3B's exact denominator terms)
contradicts_option: RelBias_c as the sole exact-null metric (OD-005 -- explicitly undefined at n_c=0 per this source)
notes: Accessed via open PMC mirror (PMC6492164) after publisher page (Wiley) returned HTTP 403. Canonical, most-cited modern reference for simulation-study design in the biostatistics literature; ADEMP framework.

full_citation: Pawel S, Bartos F, Siepe BS, Lohmann A. Handling Missingness, Failures, and Non-Convergence in Simulation Studies: A Review of Current Practices and Recommendations. The American Statistician. 2025 (accepted 2025-07-21; published online 2025-09-30).
claim_supported: EXPLICIT SOURCE CLAIM (from full-text PDF, arXiv v3): excluding failed/non-converged replications from the denominator of a performance measure (a 'complete-case'-style computation) can bias results when failures are informative -- i.e. related to the parameter values being estimated -- and the paper recommends always reporting failure/non-convergence rates alongside point estimates and CIs for performance measures, adapting an MCAR/MAR/MNAR-style classification to simulation-failure mechanisms.
exact_relevant_methodological_point: States explicitly: 'excluding failed replications artificially inflates performance' when failures are non-random.
model_assumptions: Frequentist Monte Carlo simulation-study framework; explicitly extends/builds on the Morris et al. (2019) ADEMP framework by adding failure-handling guidance to the Performance-measures step.
applicability_to_model_3b: Directly relevant to OD-006: raises a genuine methodological caution against Model 3B's already-frozen NUM-DEC-01/02 convention of using R_valid,c/R_metric,c (a valid-only, i.e. complete-case-style) denominator for Coverage_hat, IF M2's optimizer/profile-likelihood/bootstrap failures turn out to be informative (correlated with n_c, e.g. near the n=0 boundary or under weak beta identification) -- a scenario NUM-DEC-01's own text already anticipates by requiring FailureRate_c to be reported alongside every metric.
limitations: Content extracted from the arXiv preprint PDF (version available at fetch time), not the final American Statistician typeset version -- DOI resolves to the same work, but exact final wording was not independently re-verified against the publisher's typeset PDF. Does not analyze Hawkes-process or point-process recovery specifically.
supports_option: CoverAndValid_c-style attempted-denominator reporting as a caution/complement to Coverage_c (OD-006) -- this source does not by itself select one metric as 'the' primary; it argues for disclosure and caution rather than mandating a single denominator.
contradicts_option: an unqualified, disclosure-free use of Coverage_c (valid-only denominator) without also reporting FailureRate_c and without checking whether failures are informative
notes: Directly creates an adversarial/limiting tension against the field's older complete-case-by-default convention (see E-003); this tension is the central adversarial-evidence finding for OD-006 (see WAVE_2_OD_005_006_015_ADJUDICATION_READINESS_REPORT.md S9).

full_citation: Sandve GK, Nekrutenko A, Taylor J, Hovig E. Ten Simple Rules for Reproducible Computational Research. PLOS Computational Biology. 2013;9(10):e1003285.
claim_supported: EXPLICIT SOURCE CLAIMS (Rule 1): 'for every involved step, you should ensure that every detail that may influence the execution of the step is recorded' (provenance from result back to process).
